findings: New raw lines 194-217 replace the old raw lines 193-229 flat country list with an 18-region preview matrix of payment versus transfer support and permitted lock durations. EU is an aggregate row, so its appearance does not prove withdrawal from individual EU countries formerly enumerated.

Both old raw lines 186-191 and new raw lines 187-192 put INR in Group 1, whereas current source line 43 and concept line 43 put INR in Group 2. This is an existing-summary error, not a new raw change; correct currency examples without assuming eligibility of a particular account.

These examples do not establish interchangeability across surfaces or a beta SDK requirement for direct curl.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/custom/localize-prices/fx-quotes-api, the preview FX Quotes API returns current or time-locked rates for requested currency pairs, with exchange_rate, base_rate, fees, lock expiry and status. A merchant requests a quote through the server-side secret-key example and can attach its identity to a PaymentIntent or Transfer where supported; expiry or drift invalidation requires a new quote, and attachment can return a 400 with resource-specific error. The beta Ruby SDK example uses 2025-07-30.preview while direct curl uses 2025-03-31.preview; these routes do not establish interchangeability or a beta SDK requirement for curl (old raw lines 35-59, 174-229; new raw lines 36-60, 175-217). The new capture adds a region, usage-type and lock-duration matrix; the old capture gave only a country list. The mapped source-stripe-fx-quotes-api.md retains the dated flat list, omits canonical URL and new raw provenance, and has an INR fee-group error (source lines 1-20, 43). Preview access, supported MCCs, account eligibility and currency pairs remain conditional; quoting or attaching is no proof of payment or transfer outcome.
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/custom/localize-prices/fx-quotes-api, the substantive change is the old flat country list becoming an explicit payment/transfer duration matrix and the scope wording changing from currencies supported for locking to currencies supported by the API (old raw lines 186-229; new raw lines 187-217). Table spacing, Markdown emphasis, heading wording, and the interest/register snippet at new raw lines 219-229 are presentation or navigation/contact changes, not proof of live access. Retain the old list as dated evidence in source-stripe-fx-quotes-api.md while adding exact canonical URL and both raw provenance entries. Warn reciprocally that the source and linked concept misclassify INR, narrow natural expiry to drift and repeat an amount=125 minor-unit example despite prose saying 125 USD; concept line 17 also falsely makes the merchant fee universally 0%/duration-only although the merchant can absorb the FX fee via base_rate or pass it on via exchange_rate (old raw lines 66-68, 136-166; new raw lines 67-69, 137-167; source lines 43, 57-70). Source line 17 conflates beta Ruby SDK 2025-07-30.preview with direct curl 2025-03-31.preview; neither version is shown interchangeable across routes, and the SDK is not a prerequisite for direct curl. Secret-key requests are server-side, and a rate quote, client display or PaymentIntent request does not establish eligibility, successful payment, settlement or a guaranteed locked outcome.
